title: Biohazards From Sewage and Infectious Waste
summary: Workers near wastewater, sewer lines, or medical waste should treat every surface as contaminated. This talk covers protective gear, hygiene, and wound care to prevent infection.
talking_points: Assume all surfaces are contaminated when you work around sewage, wastewater, or medical waste. Avoid direct contact.
Wear waterproof gloves, boots, and face protection for direct contact with sewage. Add a face shield if splashing is possible.
Wash your hands well before eating or drinking and when the job is done.
Clean, treat, and report any cut or wound right away.
Keep contaminated gloves, boots, and gear away from areas where food is eaten or stored. Remove contaminated clothing at the site if you can.
Wash contaminated clothing at 160 degrees F or hotter. Use robotic cameras for pipe inspections when possible to cut human contact.
site_hazards_to_check: Standing sewage, wastewater, or sludge in the work area
Missing waterproof gloves, boots, or face and splash protection
No handwashing station or clean water near the work area
Food or drink stored or eaten near contaminated gear
Open cuts or wounds on workers about to enter the area
discussion_questions: What protective gear do you need before you touch anything in this space?
Where will you wash your hands and store your contaminated boots and gloves?
What do you do if you get a cut while working around raw sewage?

flags: OSHA mapping adequate: 29 CFR 1910.1030 (bloodborne pathogens) applies to the infectious / medical-waste content; for raw sewage without blood or OPIM the operative authority is 29 CFR 1926.28 (PPE) plus the General Duty Clause - both are reasonable cites. Content - treat all surfaces as contaminated, waterproof gloves/boots/face and splash protection, hand hygiene before eating and after work, prompt cut/wound care and reporting, keep contaminated gear away from food areas, hot-water laundering, use robotic cameras to cut contact - is sound. The 160 F laundry-disinfection figure matches CDC guidance.
Non-blocking enhancement: add 29 CFR 1926.51(f) (washing facilities) and 1926.51(a) (potable water) given the emphasis on handwashing stations.
